headline: TTWO and PLS surge on the Gold Coast Sunday — Iran's Hormuz standoff keeps oil elevated, gold hits record highs, and the RBA decision looms large this week.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a cracking session today, up 6.5% to $4.58. Lithium carbonate prices are holding firm around 142,750 yuan — a sign the worst of the lithium selloff may be easing. Still well down from where it was bought, but today's bounce is encouraging for long-term holders.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two jumped 6% last night in the US. The buzz is around GTA 6 — reports that Rockstar will market the game as a single-player experience first (delaying GTA Online) actually reassured investors, as it means the studio is focused on delivering a polished launch title rather than fragmenting their effort.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF slipped 0.87% today to close at $16.01, dragged by a soft session for tech-heavy AI names on the ASX. Nothing fundamental has changed — the ETF tracks global AI companies and remains subject to daily swings. Still carrying a paper loss overall, but the long-term AI story is intact.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 0.88% last night in the US to $353.47 — a modest pullback with no clear negative catalyst. Interestingly, S&P 500 earnings season has been exceptionally strong even without Alphabet dragging it higher, suggesting broader market health. Long-term thesis for Google remains solid.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: A tiny dip of 0.11% today — essentially flat. Emerging markets were quiet on the ASX. The Iran/Hormuz situation is worth watching for its impact on Asian energy importers, but there's no material shift here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Virtually unchanged today at $539.72, down just 4 cents. The underlying US market (NASDAQ +1.3%, S&P +0.62% last night) is performing well — the ASX-listed version just lags a day behind. Looking good for this holding heading into the week.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Barely moved today — up 3 cents to $77.93. VDHG is a globally diversified 'set and forget' ETF, so small daily moves are completely normal. Steady as she goes.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was essentially flat last night at just under $500 — consolidating after a big recent run driven by its Azure cloud division beating revenue expectations and raising growth guidance by 15%. The stock is hovering just below the psychologically significant $500 mark. Analysts at Simply Wall St reckon earnings suggest it may still be undervalued at current prices.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Hold after today's 6.5% bounce
watch_today.detail: Pilbara surged today on firmer lithium prices (carbonate holding at 142,750 yuan). It's still deep in the red overall (down 32% from your average buy price), but the long-term thesis — EV battery demand for lithium — hasn't changed. Don't chase today's move. Sit tight and let the recovery play out.

watch_today.title: TTWO — Hold after last night's 6% jump
watch_today.detail: Take-Two had a cracker of a session last night on GTA 6 hype. Reports say Rockstar is focusing on a polished single-player launch before GTA Online — markets liked that. You're now up 6.17% overall on this one. No reason to sell into strength — the GTA 6 launch catalyst is still ahead of you. Long-term hold.

watch_today.title: RBA interest rate decision this week — watch closely
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank is expected to announce a rate decision this week, and analysts are already warning Australians to 'buckle up' — the rate relief may be short-lived. The RBA has gone quiet on forward guidance (meaning it's stopped telegraphing future moves), adding uncertainty. Lower rates are generally good for growth stocks and ETFs like VDHG and VTS — keep an eye on Tuesday's announcement.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Hold despite ongoing loss
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF is down 15.2% overall and slipped another 0.87% today. However, the AI sector story is as strong as ever — the White House is holding a safety summit this week with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and regulatory attention actually signals the sector's importance. No structural reason to sell. This is a long-term bet on AI — hold.

watch_today.title: Gold hits record highs — tailwind for VDHG
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 3.72% last night to nearly US$4,400/oz — an extraordinary level. This reflects investor anxiety about the Iran/Hormuz standoff and geopolitical uncertainty. Gold exposure sits inside diversified ETFs like VDHG. If tensions escalate further, gold could keep climbing.

watch_today.title: Iran-Hormuz standoff keeping oil elevated
watch_today.detail: Crude oil is at US$78.18, up 1.15% last night. Iran is blocking US ships in the Strait of Hormuz — the world's most important oil chokepoint — and a deal is reportedly 'close but not enough' to reopen it. Higher oil means higher fuel and transport costs here in Australia. Worth watching this week for any escalation or resolution.

world.summary: The big global story this weekend is the Iran-US standoff in the Strait of Hormuz — one of the world's most critical oil shipping lanes — with Iran blocking US ships and oil prices rising as a result. Meanwhile, the Trump administration's targeting of political opponents continues to make headlines.

stories.title: Iran blocking US ships as Strait of Hormuz standoff escalates
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has moved to block US navy vessels in the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil passes every day. Iran says a deal is 'close' but insists other conditions must be met before the strait reopens. The standoff has pushed crude oil prices up to US$78/barrel, which flows through to petrol prices at the bowser here in Australia. If it escalates further, energy costs globally could spike sharply.

stories.title: Iran plots to keep Trump entangled in conflict heading into US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The Guardian reports that Iran is deliberately prolonging the Hormuz standoff as a strategic play — keeping the US bogged down in a Middle East conflict ahead of the November midterm elections, where Republicans are vulnerable. The theory is that a messy, unresolved war drags on Trump politically and gives Democrats a key issue. It means this dispute may not be resolved quickly, keeping oil and gold prices elevated for weeks.

stories.title: Iran sees an opening to push the US out of the Persian Gulf
stories.why_it_matters: The WSJ reports that Iran sees the current standoff as a generational opportunity to permanently reduce US military presence in the Persian Gulf. By controlling the Hormuz chokepoint, Iran gains enormous leverage — not just over the US, but over all nations dependent on Gulf oil, including Japan, South Korea, and China. A sustained US withdrawal from the region would reshape global energy security and geopolitics for decades.

stories.title: Trump administration targets James Comey and others with investigation
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has released a list of individuals it is targeting with investigations and legal action — including former FBI Director James Comey, who was fired by Trump in 2017. The list suggests the administration is using government power to pursue perceived political opponents, which critics are calling an abuse of the justice system. This is being closely watched by US allies, including Australia, as a test of American democratic norms.

stories.title: Gold surges to record US$4,400/oz as global uncertainty spikes
stories.why_it_matters: Gold hit US$4,399 per ounce last night — a gain of nearly 3.72% in a single session. When investors are scared about wars, political instability, or economic shocks, they pile into gold as a 'safe haven' asset. The combination of the Iran standoff, elevated US political tensions, and uncertainty around global trade is driving this surge. For Australian investors, gold exposure in diversified ETFs like VDHG benefits from this trend.

markets.summary: US markets had a solid night last night — the NASDAQ jumped 1.3% and the S&P 500 gained 0.62%. The ASX 200 was virtually flat today, dipping just 0.09%. Gold is at record highs and oil is elevated due to the Iran standoff. The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly to 70.71 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Virtually flat today — the market digested a quiet local session ahead of the RBA decision this week.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid gains last night as earnings season wraps up with the biggest collective beat on record.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech stocks had a good night, with AI-related names rallying across the board.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil up on Iran blocking the Strait of Hormuz — watch this for petrol price impacts.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold at record highs — investors piling in as a safe haven amid Iran tensions and political uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar nudged up slightly — still comfortably above 70 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA rate decision is the big domestic story this week, with economists warning that any rate relief could be short-lived. Labor's budget is also drawing fire from the Opposition, who are calling it economic 'havoc'.

stories.title: RBA rate relief this week could be brief — Australians told to 'buckle up'
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank is expected to deliver its interest rate decision this week, and while markets are pricing in some relief (a cut or a hold), economists are already warning that any easing could be short-lived. Australia is still dealing with stubborn services inflation and a tight labour market. Mortgage holders hoping for a sustained run of rate cuts may be disappointed — the advice is to budget conservatively.

stories.title: The RBA has gone silent — what it means when the central bank stops talking
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports that the RBA has abandoned its practice of 'forward guidance' — basically, it's stopped telling the public what it expects to do with rates in future meetings. The RBA says the economy is too uncertain to make promises. This makes it much harder for borrowers and businesses to plan ahead. It also means each RBA meeting will now carry more market-moving surprise potential.

stories.title: ASX set to hit record high as earnings season and RBA decision collide
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR says the ASX is poised to challenge record highs this week, with a combination of strong earnings results and the RBA decision potentially acting as catalysts. A rate cut — or even a dovish (rates-staying-low-friendly) signal from the RBA — could push Australian shares higher. Key earnings reports from major ASX companies are also due, making this a potentially big week for your portfolio.

stories.title: Labor's budget branded economic 'havoc' by Shadow Treasurer
stories.why_it_matters: Opposition Shadow Treasurer has slammed the Labor government's budget as destined to create economic 'havoc', ramping up political pressure ahead of what's shaping up as a tough week for the government. The critique centres on spending levels and their potential to keep inflation elevated — which could in turn pressure the RBA to keep rates higher for longer. This is the central tension in Australian economic policy right now: the government spends, the RBA tightens.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the dominant theme this week — the White House is convening a safety summit with the major AI labs, Australia is wrestling with copyright law reform, and the Trump administration is pushing back on Congressional attempts to rein in AI. Meanwhile, deals offering access to multiple AI models for a flat fee are doing the rounds.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google called to White House AI safety summit
stories.why_it_matters: The White House is hosting a high-stakes meeting with the bosses of OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), and Google (Gemini) to discuss AI safety. This is a signal that the US government is taking AI risks seriously at the highest level — the conversation will likely touch on deepfakes, autonomous weapons, and economic disruption from automation. The outcome could shape regulation that affects companies like Alphabet (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT), which are in your portfolio.

stories.title: Australia's shifting approach to copyright and AI — what it means for creators
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is rethinking how copyright law applies to AI — specifically, whether AI companies can legally use books, articles, music, and artwork to train their models without paying for it. Right now they mostly can, but Australian regulators are moving to tighten the rules. This matters for Australian creators (writers, artists, musicians) who currently get nothing when their work is used to train AI, and for AI companies operating here who may face new licensing costs.

stories.title: Trump pushes back on AI regulation as Congress considers tighter controls
stories.why_it_matters: While Congress is pushing for stricter AI safety rules (things like mandatory testing before deployment, liability for AI harms), the Trump White House is resisting, arguing that heavy-handed regulation would put the US behind China in the AI race. This tension — innovation vs safety — is the defining political fight of the AI era. For investors in AI companies like Alphabet and Microsoft, less regulation is generally seen as a short-term positive for profits.

stories.title: Deepfake victim calls for better AI regulation after ordeal
stories.why_it_matters: A deepfake victim has gone public with the BBC, urging governments to act faster on regulating AI-generated fake images and videos. Deepfakes — realistic-looking fake videos or photos made by AI — are increasingly being used for harassment, fraud, and misinformation. The victim's case highlights a real harm that technology is enabling right now, and is adding public pressure on regulators globally (including Australia) to act.

stories.title: Get access to 20+ AI models — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and more — for a flat fee around $60-$79
stories.why_it_matters: Several services are now offering lifetime access to 20+ AI models — including ChatGPT (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic), and Gemini (Google) — via a single dashboard for a one-off payment of around US$60-$79. For everyday users, this is a practical way to access best-in-class AI tools without paying monthly subscriptions to each service separately. It's a sign the AI tools market is maturing and becoming more accessible.

sport.summary: Round 23 NRL wrapped up with the Dolphins pulling off a stunning comeback over the Broncos, the Knights booking their finals spot at the Raiders' expense, and a controversy-filled weekend of footy. In the AFL, Melbourne upset ladder-leader Fremantle in a 34-goal MCG classic.

stories.title: Dolphins defeat Broncos 40-32 in historic comeback — sin bin controversy steals headlines
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins beat the Broncos 40-32 at Suncorp Stadium in a wild one — coming from behind to win in what Fox Sports is calling a 'historic comeback'. A controversial sin bin call was the turning point, sparking debate about the game's officiating. Big result for the Dolphins and another tough night for a Broncos side struggling for consistency.

stories.title: Knights clinch finals spot, Raiders self-destruct in 'horror year'
stories.why_it_matters: Newcastle Knights beat the Canberra Raiders 30-24 in Canberra to officially book their finals spot — a big milestone for a club that's been rebuilding. The Raiders, meanwhile, had a 'brain explosion' moment late in the game that Fox Sports describes as the low point of their 'horror year'. Canberra's finals hopes are now all but over.

stories.title: Rabbitohs hold off Eels 28-24 — freak injury rocks Souths
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney beat Parramatta 28-24 in a tight one at Allianz Stadium, denying the Eels what would have been a remarkable comeback. Fox Sports reports a 'freak injury' hit Souths during the match — details pending — which could impact their finals campaign. The Eels' shot at 'all-time NRL history' (winning from a record deficit) fell just short.

stories.title: Melbourne Demons stun ladder-leading Fremantle in MCG classic
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne knocked off ladder leaders Fremantle in a 34-goal shootout at the MCG. News.com.au says the Dees 'sunk Freo' in a result that shakes up the top-of-the-table picture. Fremantle had been the form team of the competition — this loss could open the door for other clubs chasing top-four spots heading into the finals series.

stories.title: Perth Bears unveil historic jersey ahead of AFL expansion debut
stories.why_it_matters: The Perth Bears — the AFL's newest expansion team — have unveiled their inaugural jersey, which NT News is calling 'the most exciting story in Australian sport'. The Bears will join the competition as the AFL's 20th team, giving Western Australia a third club. The jersey reveal is a historic milestone for the league and marks a new era of AFL expansion into new markets.
